All models run by the maintainer on the same set; per-source WERs kept as components.
caveats: Test set is gated on Hugging Face (datasets/yagmurtuncer/turkasr-bench); public components (Common Voice, FLEURS) may overlap training data.
Maintainer also co-authors Turkish Whisper fine-tunes on the same board (not catalogue models).
Corpus WER pooled over sources, so larger/longer sources weigh more than in a per-source mean.

name: VoiceCodeBench · batch WER (300 English workplace segments)
setup: VoiceCodeBench v2 (Besimple AI): 300 human-recorded English workplace segments (5.59 h, 85 speakers) dense in structured tokens (emails, URLs, paths, commands, IDs, amounts), raw audio only (no prompts, keyterms or biasing). Batch/file APIs and local open models; corpus WER as printed in Table 5 (v2 scoring).
caveats: v1 of the paper printed very different WERs for the same runs (different WER normalisation); v2 is pinned.
Streaming configurations excluded (different products).
Hosted API aliases may change after the run dates (May-Sep 2026).
Whisper large-v3 was served by Groq (whisper-large-v3); Parakeet via transformers on Modal at a pinned HF revision.

name: VoiceCodeBench · batch canonical token/entity match (CTEM)
setup: Same batch runs as voicecodebench-batch-wer. CTEM = share of 1,482 audited target entities (26 types) whose exact canonical value is recoverable from the transcript, judged by a versioned GPT-5.5 recoverability verifier with an independent human audit. Higher is better.
caveats: LLM-verifier-based metric (audited).
Measures exact value recovery, which ranks systems differently from WER (Spearman -0.28 per source).

name: AfriCodeSwitch English-Yoruba code-switched speech · WER (cap2000)
setup: 2,000 shared utterances (cap2000) of English-Yoruba intra-sentential code-switched read speech from the AfriCodeSwitch validation corpus (100 speakers, 13 domains). Zero-shot greedy decoding; WER after NFC normalisation, case-folding and punctuation stripping (diacritic-sensitive). University of Florida authors' runs (Table II).
caveats: None of the ASR systems supports Yoruba; Yoruba-token error is 97-99% for all, so WER (66-74%) mostly reflects English-token recognition. Low discriminative range.
Whisper forced to English; the auto-language row is excluded.

name: Rime SupportBench · paired human preference vs Rime Coda (US English)
setup: Rime AlphaTTSBench v1.0.0 SupportBench: 750 US-English scripts (customer-support conversation turns (identifiers, amounts, dates, dialogue)); every competitor clip is paired with the same script rendered by Rime Coda (voice clementine). Blind US listeners on Podonos rate each pair on a five-point comparison scale with a real tie (+2 Rime much better .. -2 competitor much better); audio level-matched to -23 LUFS, 24 kHz. Ratings are averaged within script, scripts weighted equally; 95% family-clustered bootstrap intervals. One configured voice per provider (configs/provider_configs.json). Score = competitor-minus-Rime mean, so every competitor is measured against the same fixed anchor.
scale_transform: score = (d + 2) / 4, d = competitor-minus-Rime-Coda mean paired score (source reports Rime-minus-competitor; sign flipped)
display_unit: paired preference vs Rime Coda on -2..+2; 0.5 = parity with the anchor; not accuracy
caveats: Vendor-run: Rime (maker of the Coda anchor) ran all competitors; the anchor itself is not a catalogue model and gets no row.
One voice per provider; results describe these voices/configurations, not every voice of a model.
Hosted model aliases (sonic-3, gpt-4o-mini-tts, aura-2) can change server-side; collection finished before the 2026-09-12 freeze.
The protocol forbids a combined score across benchmarks; SupportBench and ContentBench are separate series.
ElevenLabs comparison is a separate 7-rating-per-script study (5,250 judgments) versus 2,730 for the others.

name: Voice-First Nation · 10 Indian languages overall pairwise preference (Bradley–Terry)
setup: 5,357 native and code-mixed sentences in Bengali, Gujarati, Hindi, Kannada, Malayalam, Marathi, Odia, Tamil, Telugu and Urdu (16 domains; normalized, symbolic and code-mixed subsets; tongue twisters and STEM stress items). Seven systems generated with their recommended default voices, non-streaming, identical prompts, no style conditioning; same-gender voice pairs. 1,915 screened and trained native raters, >120K two-step pairwise comparisons (holistic preference locked before six perceptual axes). Overall preference fit with a maximum-likelihood Bradley–Terry model mapped to an Elo-like scale; 500 bootstrap resamples for 95% CIs.
score_unit: published Bradley–Terry rating on an Elo-like scale; higher is better
caveats: Systems cover different language subsets (#lang 2-10); MiniMax Speech 2.8 HD was compared in only 2 languages (7,834 comparisons).
'Gemini 2.5 Pro TTS' (rank 1) is not mapped: the label does not pin the Gemini API preview id vs the Cloud GA id.
Bulbul v3 Beta (Sarvam) and Indic F5 are not catalogue models; their ratings anchor the scale but get no rows.
Crowd pairwise preference from a controlled rater pool (not a public arena).

name: InstructTTSEval EN · mean instruction-following score (APS, DSD, RP)
setup: InstructTTSEval English subset: 1,000 expressive reference clips, each turned into three natural-language style instructions — Acoustic-Parameter Specification (APS), Descriptive-Style Directive (DSD) and Role-Play (RP). Systems synthesize from the text plus instruction only (no prompt audio). Gemini-as-a-judge scores whether each output follows the instruction (79% agreement with human annotators on a 50-clip check). Avg. = unweighted mean of the APS, DSD and RP percentages.
caveats: LLM judge from the Gemini family also scores Gemini TTS outputs (possible self-preference).
Unmarked asterisks in the source table on gemini-flash, gemini-pro and hume.
Reference audio scores (84.3 EN / 82.5 ZH) and open instruct-TTS rows (Parler-TTS, VoxInstruct, PromptTTS, PromptStyle) not imported.

name: InstructTTSEval ZH · mean instruction-following score (APS, DSD, RP)

name: SAP voice reconstruction · human BWS reconstruction preference
setup: Voice reconstruction for people with speech disorders: 193 English-L1 speakers from the Speech Accessibility Project (Dec-2024 release; Parkinson's, cerebral palsy, ALS, Down syndrome; 39 low-intelligibility). For each speaker one disordered recording is the zero-shot cloning prompt and another utterance's transcript is synthesized (193 utterances per system, 17 open-weight zero-shot systems). Subjective: Best–Worst Scaling with situational framing ('how the speaker sounded before the condition'), 4 systems per screen incl. the recording, 5 listening tests, 47 retained Prolific listeners (UK/US, English L1, paid); Plackett–Luce worths relative to the original recording.
score_unit: Elo-like rating = 1000 + 400·log10(e)·log-worth (log-worth relative to the original recording = 0)
scale_transform: score = 1000 + 173.7178 × published log-worth (natural-log Plackett–Luce worth; original recording = 1000)
caveats: Special use case: cloning from disordered speech; not a general naturalness test.
Qwen3-TTS, Fish Speech, VibeVoice and OpenVoice rows are not mapped (checkpoint/size/version not stated).
Other rows (E2-TTS, F5-TTS, MaskGCT, VoiceCraft, GPT-SoVITS, HierSpeech, StyleTTS2, Vevo, WhisperSpeech) are not catalogue models.
The Elo-like mapping is a fixed linear rescaling of the printed log-worths (no refit); raw log-worth kept per result.

name: SAP voice reconstruction · WER of reconstructed speech (Whisper turbo)
setup: Voice reconstruction for people with speech disorders: 193 English-L1 speakers from the Speech Accessibility Project (Dec-2024 release; Parkinson's, cerebral palsy, ALS, Down syndrome; 39 low-intelligibility). name: SAP voice reconstruction · TTSDS dual-reference distributional score
setup: Voice reconstruction for people with speech disorders: 193 English-L1 speakers from the Speech Accessibility Project (Dec-2024 release; Parkinson's, cerebral palsy, ALS, Down syndrome; 39 low-intelligibility). For each speaker one disordered recording is the zero-shot cloning prompt and another utterance's transcript is synthesized (193 utterances per system, 17 open-weight zero-shot systems). name: CodecMOS-Accent VCTK voice clone · human naturalness MOS (S-NAT)
setup: VCTK accented English: 32 speakers across 10 accents (20 F / 12 M), 5 target sentences per speaker (160 per system), zero-shot cloning from a different 3-7 s utterance of the same speaker, 16 kHz. 15 open-source voice-cloning systems. Crowdsourced listening test (Intergroup): 25 listeners (19 US, 2 CA, 3 EN, 1 SCO) each rated 784 samples on 5-point scales (19,600 annotations, ~4.9 per sample); 55 unusable samples removed. S-NAT: naturalness considering pronunciation, prosody and noise.
caveats: Ground-truth VCTK scores 4.045 S-NAT (below several TTS systems) because of recording artifacts.

Orpheus-TTS not mapped (pretrained vs finetune checkpoint not stated); CosyVoice 2, Llasa-1B, VoiceStar, MaskGCT, VevoTTS, FireRedTTS, VALL-E-X were not mapped at import; NeuTTS Air was added on 2026-10-05.
Checkpoint revisions not stated; open-weight defaults assumed.

name: CodecMOS-Accent VCTK voice clone · human speaker-similarity MOS (S-SPK-SIM)
setup: VCTK accented English: 32 speakers across 10 accents (20 F / 12 M), 5 target sentences per speaker (160 per system), zero-shot cloning from a different 3-7 s utterance of the same speaker, 16 kHz. 15 open-source voice-cloning systems. setup.version: HPS v2 benchmark ('v2 benchmark' table in the README, commit 866735e); HPD v2 benchmark prompts in Animation, Concept-art, Painting and Photo styles, scored with HPS v2 (not HPS v2.1)
setup.metric: Published 'Averaged' HPS v2 score over the four styles. HPS v2 is a CLIP-based human-preference model; its score is reported x100 and stored divided by 100 (observed range about 0.23-0.28).
setup.protocol: The benchmark authors generated every model's images themselves (settings in arXiv 2306.09341v2 Appendix D) and released them with HPD v2; SDXL 0.9 rows were added in July 2023.
setup.comparability: Automatic preference-model score, not human votes. Do not pool with the README's HPS v2.1 table (same images, different scorer) or with HPS v2 values printed by other papers.

setup.version: TIFA v1.0 (4,081 prompts, 25,829 pre-generated GPT-3 questions), report v3 Appendix Table 4
setup.metric: Published Overall TIFA score: VQA accuracy of mPLUG-large on the benchmark questions for each generated image; 0-100 divided by 100.
setup.protocol: Benchmark authors' own generations and scoring (Sec. 5.2, Appendix E).
setup.comparability: Automatic VQA faithfulness score; not the TIFA160 human Likert ratings and not the image-only leaderboard in the repository. About two thirds of questions are yes/no, so the practical floor is well above 0.

setup.version: GenAI-Arena report v3, Table 5(a); leaderboard last updated 4 June 2024; the full pool of 10 text-to-image models at that date
setup.metric: Elo rating from anonymous pairwise human votes on the authors' arena; 95% CI kept in notes.
setup.protocol: Prompts sampled from ImagenHub; models served through ImagenHub wrappers with the resolutions and step counts of Table 2; checkpoints per the arena's model registry.
setup.comparability: Relative to this 10-model pool; not LMArena and not GEditBench Elo. The v4 (Oct 2024) top-10 table is a later snapshot of the same arena and is not imported.

setup.version: ImagenHub report v4 (10 Mar 2024), Table 4, Text-guided Image Generation block
setup.metric: Published Overall human score: average over images of sqrt(SC x PQ), where SC (semantic consistency) and PQ (perceptual quality) are rated 0 / 0.5 / 1; already 0-1.
setup.protocol: Default settings from official implementations or Hugging Face docs, negative prompts and prompt engineering disabled; three raters per model (Prolific and the authors); ImagenHub standardized prompt set.
setup.comparability: Human ratings on ImagenHub's own prompt set; do not pool with the editing or subject-driven blocks, or with automatic CLIP scores in the same table.

name: EvalMuse-40K model ranking (FGA-BLIP2 overall alignment)

setup.version: EvalMuse-40K report v2 (25 Dec 2024), Appendix Table 10
setup.metric: Published overall image-text alignment score predicted by the authors' FGA-BLIP2 model on the 1-5 Likert scale of the EvalMuse annotations; stored as (score - 1) / 4.
setup.protocol: 200 representative prompts; images generated by the authors for each model; single automatic scorer.
setup.comparability: Automatic alignment metric trained on EvalMuse human labels, not a human rating of these images. Per-skill columns are correlated tracks and are not imported.

display_unit: FGA-BLIP2 predicted alignment / 5; not human MOS

setup.version: Kolors README Human Assessment table (April 2024 product versions); protocol in the Kolors technical report (imgs/Kolors_paper.pdf, same commit)
setup.metric: Average Overall Satisfaction on a 1-5 scale (holistic rating with the prompt shown); stored as (score - 1) / 4.
setup.protocol: KolorsPrompts (over 1,000 prompts, 14 categories); about 50 professional reviewers; four images per prompt, each rated five times; 1024x1024; Kolors prompted in Chinese, other models in English.
setup.limitations: Evaluator is the maker of Kolors (Kolors row is lab). Visual Appeal and Text Faithfulness columns are correlated tracks of the same study and are not imported.

setup.version: ConceptMix v1 (arXiv 2408.14339v1), Table 4, difficulty k=2
setup.metric: Full-mark score: share of generated images that satisfy all k+1 = 3 sampled visual concepts, graded by GPT-4o; already 0-1.
setup.protocol: 300 prompts per k generated with GPT-4o from sampled concepts (objects, colors, numbers, shapes, sizes, textures, spatial relations, styles); open models from the Hugging Face checkpoints in Table 8; DALL·E 3 via API defaults.
setup.comparability: Only k=2 is imported; k=1..7 are correlated difficulty levels of the same run (k=2 chosen as the middle of the non-floor range). Automatic GPT-4o grading.

name: Picovoice STT benchmark · English batch 4-set mean WER
setup: Picovoice/speech-to-text-benchmark README (Apache-2.0) at 43e7689: unweighted mean of LibriSpeech test-clean, LibriSpeech test-other, TED-LIUM and Common Voice (English) WER as printed in the 'Average' column; Picovoice's own normalizer; batch (non-streaming) engines on CPU. Different sets and normalizer from the Open ASR averages.

setup.version: Leaderboard snapshot arena_elo/results/20250322 (identical to results/latest) at Space revision 4197b3a
setup.metric: 'Arena Elo rating (anony)': Elo from anonymous public pairwise votes, computed by the maintainers' FastChat-derived arena_elo scripts; the Space displays this column (serve/leaderboard.py)
setup.protocol: Public users submit a prompt; two anonymous models generate short clips (about 2-5 s) and the user votes. Models served through VideoGenHub (TIGER-AI-Lab, arena branch) or fal.ai endpoints listed in model/model_registry.py.
setup.limitations: Pool of 15 mostly 2024 open models; ratings are relative to this pool and not on Arena's scale. Several models were retired from active battles before the snapshot. Allegro ran with 20 steps instead of its default 100.

setup.version: VideoPhy-1 human leaderboard, repository commit 01d366c
setup.metric: Percentage of test prompts whose video is judged by human annotators to follow the caption (SA=1) and intuitive physics (PC=1); divided by 100.
setup.protocol: VideoPhy-1 test captions (solid-solid, solid-fluid, fluid-fluid interactions); videos generated by the benchmark authors; human annotation (Appendix K of arXiv 2406.03520 lists per-model resolution/frames/steps).
setup.limitations: Not the VideoPhy-1 auto-evaluator track (videophy-autoeval-avg) and not VideoPhy-2. Same videos as the auto track, so the two are correlated.

setup.version: AIGVE-60K / LOVE, arXiv 2505.12098v1, Table 8 'Overall' column
setup.metric: Model-level mean of per-video perception MOS; each rater's scores converted to z-scores and rescaled by 100(z+3)/6, then averaged over raters; divided by 100.
setup.protocol: 3,050 prompts across 20 task dimensions, 58,500 videos from 30 T2V models generated by the authors (commercial products accessed 2025-03-08), 15 annotators per video, ITU-R BT.500 outlier rejection.
setup.limitations: Rescaled z-scores are relative to this pool, not an absolute quality scale. Perception and correspondence MOS rate the same videos and are correlated. Commercial rows without a version are not imported.

setup.version: AIGVE-60K / LOVE, arXiv 2505.12098v1, Table 9 'Overall' column
setup.metric: Model-level mean of per-video text-video correspondence MOS (z-scores rescaled by 100(z+3)/6); divided by 100.
setup.protocol: Same 58,500 videos and annotation campaign as the perception MOS.
setup.limitations: Correlated with the perception track (same videos and raters). Commercial rows without a version are not imported.

setup.version: WorldModelBench, arXiv 2502.20694v1, Table 3 (human annotations)
setup.metric: Total score out of 10 (instruction following 0-3, common sense frame/temporal 0-2, five physics laws 0-5), averaged over prompts; divided by 10.
setup.protocol: 350 image+text condition pairs over 7 application domains; T2V models get the re-captioned text, I2V models the first frame plus text; authors' own generations with each model's recommended settings (Appendix 8.3); 67K human labels, up to 3 voters per video.
setup.limitations: T2V and I2V models share one table; the conditioning is recorded per row. Judge-model scores (Table 9) and the Hard subset are not imported.

setup.version: Seaweed-7B technical report, arXiv 2504.08685v2, Table 3
setup.metric: Elo from side-by-side human votes on overall fidelity (win ratio retained in note).
setup.protocol: MagicArena (ByteDance) pairwise evaluation: >500 raters, each model in >=7,000 comparisons; baseline videos generated with each model's official API as of early March 2025; Seaweed-7B at 480p/720p.
setup.limitations: Evaluation run by the Seaweed developer (Seaweed-7B row is lab). Eight-model pool; ratings not on Arena's scale. Wan 2.1 and HunyuanVideo rows not imported (API vs checkpoint identity unclear).

setup.version: VideoVerse, arXiv 2510.08398v4 (15 May 2026), Table 1
setup.metric: Published Overall points (793 binary hidden-semantics questions + event-following LCS over 815 events) divided by 1608.
setup.protocol: 300 prompts with 10 dimensions (event following, camera control, interaction, mechanics, material properties, natural constraints, common sense, attributes, 2D layout, 3D depth); Gemini 2.5 Pro evaluator validated by a user study (Table 3). Open models run by the authors on A800s; closed models via official APIs (Veo-3-fast, Sora-2 standard).
setup.limitations: VLM-judged; 5 s short-video setting used where two settings exist. Sora-2 missing 4 videos.

setup.version: ChronoMagic-Bench-150 subset, arXiv 2406.18522v2 Table 4
setup.metric: GPT4o-MTScore: GPT-4o rates the metamorphic amplitude (how fully the requested time-lapse transformation happens) of uniformly sampled frames on a 5-point scale; model mean stored as value/5 with chance 0.2 mapping the scale floor to zero.
setup.protocol: 150 time-lapse prompts (biological, human-created, meteorological, physical); three videos per prompt; open models run by the authors with official code and default settings (Appendix D lists resolution/frames); closed products generated in June 2024.
setup.limitations: Specialised to time-lapse/metamorphic prompts and scored by a GPT-4o judge (human agreement checked in Fig. 6). UMTScore, MTScore, CHScore and UMT-FVD from the same videos are not imported.

name: Seed-TTS test-en · speaker similarity (WavLM-large SV)

name: TTSDS2 listening test · naturalness MOS (4 English domains)
setup: TTSDS2 study (Minixhofer et al.): 20 open-weight voice-cloning systems (2022-2024 releases, latest checkpoint before 2025-01-01) synthesise 60 speakers per domain in four English domains: Clean (LibriTTS test), Noisy (LibriTTS with added noise), Wild (YouTube speech) and Kids (children's speech). The first utterance of each speaker is the reference, the transcript of a second utterance is synthesised. Prolific listeners (UK/US native speakers, headphones, three attention checks passed; ~50 per domain, one domain each) rate naturalness on a 5-point Bad-Excellent scale. Score = unweighted mean over the four domains of the per-domain mean rating, computed by us from the individual ratings (rating_type=mos). This reproduces the paper's Table 2 MOS column to two decimals for every system.
caveats: Ground-truth ratings are not published (licensing); the paper reports ground truth at MOS 3.70, so absolute MOS levels are survey-specific.
Each MOS page mixes one ground-truth clip with four random systems; roughly 200-280 ratings per system in total.
ParlerTTS was run through a codebase modification to allow voice cloning (paper Appendix A).

name: TTSDS2 listening test · speaker-similarity MOS (4 English domains)

Score = unweighted mean over Clean/Noisy/Wild/Kids of the per-domain mean rating (rating_type=smos), computed by us from the individual ratings; reproduces the paper's Table 2 SMOS column to two decimals.
caveats: Voice-cloning fidelity, not naturalness; same listeners and samples as the MOS benchmark.
Ground-truth SMOS 4.37 in the paper (not published in the dataset).

name: TTSDS2 multilingual benchmark · English overall (YouTube, 2025 round)
setup: TTSDS2 multilingual round published May 2025 (ttsds/leaderboard_data). The TTSDS2 pipeline collects YouTube talk-show/interview/news/podcast speech uploaded after the newest evaluated system was published, diarises it with Whisper, filters controversial content, crosstalk and music, and keeps 50 speaker-matched utterance pairs per language (reference set / synthesis set). Every system clones each reference speaker and speaks the paired transcript. Multilingual TTSDS2 (mHuBERT-147 / XLS-R features) scores each factor 0-100 by distance to the held-out real speech ('Ground Truth A') versus noise distributions; OVERALL is the unweighted mean of SPEAKER, PROSODY, INTELLIGIBILITY and GENERIC. A second real-speech set ('Ground Truth B en') scores 91.63. Divided by 100.
caveats: Distribution similarity to real speech, not recognition accuracy or MOS; distinct from TTSDS v1 and from ZTTS1's TTSDS2 prosody factor.
Same 20 systems as the TTSDS2 listening test; XTTS and VoiceCraft-830M not mapped.
Scores are clustered (79-90); small differences are within run-to-run noise.

setup.version: GeckoNum, arXiv 2406.14774v3, Table 2 Task 1 column
setup.metric: Share of image-question pairs where the annotated object count equals the number in the prompt (per-response binary accuracy averaged); percentage divided by 100. Random chance 10.0 per the table.
setup.protocol: Numeric-simple, attribute and compositional count prompts (Task 1 of 3); five images per model and prompt (five seeds); each image annotated by five paid participants; counts pre-processed as in Appendix C.2.
setup.comparability: Only Task 1 is imported; Tasks 2 (approximate/zero) and 3 (conceptual) are separate, correlated tasks of the same study. Standard errors (~0.4-0.5 pp) kept in notes.

setup.version: WorldReasonBench / WorldRewardBench, arXiv 2605.10434v1, Table 4 'Human Elo'
setup.metric: Elo-scale ability from a Bradley-Terry model with Davidson ties fitted to expert pairwise preferences (Appendix G; 1,000 prompt-cluster bootstrap resamples for CIs).
setup.protocol: 436 TI2V cases (initial image + instruction; 4 reasoning dimensions, 22 sub-categories); WorldRewardBench subset: 11 generators, 8 videos sampled per case, 15 trained annotators rate reasoning quality, temporal consistency and aesthetics on 1-5 (S = 0.4 s_r + 0.3 s_c + 0.3 s_a), ranked within case into ~6K preference pairs over ~1.4K videos (near-equal pairs as ties). Closed models via their commercial APIs; open models with each official inference recipe, 480p-720p clips.
setup.limitations: Ratings are relative to this 11-generator pool, not LMArena's scale. Pairs are derived from absolute 1-5 ratings rather than direct side-by-side votes. Kling and UniVideo rows are not imported; Sora 2 at 12 s is a second setting of the same model.

Same sets and normalizer as picovoice-en4-batch-avg-wer but a different decoding condition (streaming), so a separate series.

name: HEIM text-image alignment (aspect win rate, v1.1.0)

setup.version: HEIM v1.1.0 as summarised in arXiv 2311.04287v1 Table 5 (26-model pool)

setup.protocol: Zero-shot FID on 30k MS-COCO 2014 validation captions, outputs unified to 256x256, optimal classifier-free guidance chosen by grid search over [1.5, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0, 5.0] (Sec. 2.3, Table 1 caption); computed by the ImageReward authors

setup.version: VVRBench main split as released with arXiv:2609.35641v1 (28 Sep 2026): 10,000 tasks, complexity 3-48, 32 constraint types
setup.metric: Task accuracy: share of tasks whose generated image passes every constraint (counts, attributes, sizes, spatial relations) under the deterministic, reference-free pixel-to-object verifier; reported in %, stored /100.
setup.protocol: VVRBench main split, 10,000 programmatically generated tasks of structural complexity 3-48 over 32 constraint types; a generated image succeeds only if every constraint passes the deterministic pixel-to-object verifier; accuracy = mean success over tasks. Open-weight models at Table 9 settings (steps/CFG); API models at medium quality 1024x1024; responses without an image count as failures.
setup.limitations: Synthetic geometric-object scenes only (precise instruction following, not aesthetics). Do not pool with VVRBench-Fast (820-task subset) or VVRBench-Challenge. Near-zero scores for weak models are at the floor.

setup.protocol: VVRBench-Challenge, 720 tasks of complexity 45-80 (20 per integer complexity) adding 14 group-level constraint types; same deterministic verifier and all-constraints-pass accuracy. API models only: GPT models at medium quality 1024x1024, Gemini models at 1K (Table 9); responses without an image count as failures.

setup.version: ChartSync as released with arXiv:2607.10301v1 (11 Jul 2026): 870 triplets, Table 2
setup.metric: Overall = equal average of OCR F1, SSIM, TESR, VLCS and BFS (each 0-100), stored /100. VLM-judged parts use Gemini-3.1-Pro at temperature 0.1.
setup.protocol: ChartSync: 870 expert-validated chart-editing triplets (9 chart categories, 4 task types, 235 geometry-coupled VLCE instances); each model edits the source chart image per instruction; Overall = equal average of five metric-level scores: OCR F1 and SSIM against the programmatic ground truth, and Gemini-3.1-Pro judged TESR (text edit success), VLCS (visuo-logical consistency, VLCE subset only) and BFS (background fidelity).
setup.limitations: Charts only (statistical-chart text and geometry edits). Mixes pixel metrics with a single VLM judge; VLCS covers only the 235 VLCE items. Metric-level summary, not a per-sample average.

setup.version: InfoEdit as released with arXiv:2609.33286v1 (27 Sep 2026): 1,000 infographics x 4 edit tasks
setup.metric: Avg. = mean over the four tasks of success rate (edit compliance AND content preservation, judged by Gemini-3.1-Pro); %, stored /100.
setup.protocol: InfoEdit: 1,000 rendered infographics (eight logical-relation families) x four reflow-requiring edit tasks (Expand-Text, Insert-Element, Swap-Block, Reshape-Canvas) = 4,000 edits; a sample succeeds (SR) only if both edit compliance and content preservation pass under the Gemini-3.1-Pro judge (validated against human majority votes, Appendix E); Avg. = mean SR over the four tasks.
setup.limitations: Infographic layouts only; single MLLM judge; most models are near the floor (0-5%), so the run mainly separates frontier models.

setup.version: PaintBench as released with arXiv:2606.00188v1 (29 May 2026), baseline visual conditions, Table 1
setup.metric: Benchmark Avg.: macro-average over 20 tasks of mean IoU (%) between the model's edit and the deterministic ground truth; stored /100.
setup.protocol: PaintBench: procedurally generated single-answer editing problems (20 task types in four categories: geometric transformation, structural manipulation, color change, symbolic reasoning) at 1024x1024 baseline conditions; deterministic pixel-level scoring of the edited image against the programmatic ground truth (mean IoU over edit classes), no judge model; Benchmark Avg. = macro-average over the 20 tasks.
setup.limitations: Synthetic shapes/colours on plain backgrounds; precise single-answer edits rather than open-ended editing quality; best model 17.1%, most near the floor.

setup.version: MechVerse test split as released with arXiv:2605.14843v1 (14 May 2026), Table 1 WorldModelBench columns
setup.metric: Sum of WorldModelBench judge scores (instruction 0-3, physics 0-5, common sense 0-2), out of 10; stored /10.
setup.protocol: MechVerse test split: image-to-video generation of mechanical assemblies (gears, linkages, cam-follower, pistons, multi-part mechanisms) from a first frame plus a structured motion prompt; default inference settings per model; outputs scored with the WorldModelBench MLLM judge: instruction following (0-3) + physics (0-5) + common sense (0-2) = Sum (0-10).
setup.limitations: MLLM judge; the authors report that judge scores rise with mechanism complexity while human-rated motion correctness falls, so the judge is lenient on part-level kinematic errors. VBench-I2V columns in the same table are separate automatic metrics and are not imported.

setup.protocol: MindWorldBench: 744 expert-designed image-to-video prompts in which a character's mental state (belief, desire, perception) should determine one of two candidate actions; each I2V system generates one video per prompt; Gemini 3.1 Pro judges with a structured multi-step rubric pipeline (validated on 100 videos against 10 human experts); Intention Accuracy = % of prompts whose generated action follows the intention implied by the mental-state condition.
setup.limitations: Single VLM judge; the benchmark's other columns (visual quality, commonsense plausibility 1-5; world-state maintenance %) are not imported. Two candidate actions per prompt, so a model ignoring the mental state can still hit the intended action by chance.

setup.protocol: ViGoR-Bench: zero-shot visual reasoning tasks (physical, knowledge and symbolic reasoning; 20 subdomains, e.g. mazes, sudoku, science phenomena) posed to image-editing/unified models (input image + instruction) and video generators (reasoning sequence, final frame scored); Gemini-2.5-Pro judges against ground-truth references (validated on a 1,080-output split against three human experts). Result Metric Avg = mean of BC, RO, VQ and RS (%).
setup.limitations: Only the final frame of each generated video is scored by the Result metric; Process metrics (whole sequence) not imported. Single VLM judge.

setup.version: PhyGround as released with arXiv:2605.10806v1 (11 May 2026), Table 2, 250 ti2v prompts
setup.metric: Overall human score on a 1-5 scale (equal weight of general adherence and physics-domain views), stored /5 with chance 0.2.
setup.protocol: PhyGround: 250 text+image-to-video prompts (first frame given; sources VideoPhy-2, Physics-IQ, OpenVid, WorldModelBench) covering 13 physics laws; each model generates one video per prompt at its native default settings (2,000 videos); 352 quality-controlled human annotators rate 1-5 semantic alignment, physical temporal validity, persistence and the applicable physics laws; Overall = equal-weight combination of the general and physics-domain views.
setup.limitations: Only 8 models; native default settings per model (resolution/fps differ); human means of 2.5-3.3 sit in a narrow band. Sub-dimension columns and the PhyJudge automatic scores are not imported.

name: EdiVal multi-turn editing overall (EdiVal-O after turn 3)

setup.version: EdiVal-Agent report v3 (17 Mar 2026), Table 3, 16 editors
setup.metric: EdiVal-O after the third sequential edit: geometric mean of EdiVal-IF and EdiVal-CC (0-100), the column the table ranks by; stored /100.
setup.protocol: EdiVal-Bench multi-turn editing: each model applies three sequential object-centric edit instructions (T1-T3) per image with default settings (APIs or official repos); EdiVal-IF (instruction following via Qwen2.5-VL-7B plus Grounding DINO checks) and EdiVal-CC (content consistency via DINOv3 features) are combined by geometric mean into EdiVal-O; the table ranks models by EdiVal-O after turn 3.
setup.limitations: Automatic object-centric pipeline (detector + small VLM), not human ratings; turn-1/turn-2 values and the perceptual-quality table (Table 4) are not imported.

setup.version: WEAVEBench as released with arXiv:2511.11434v1 (14 Nov 2025), Table 2
setup.metric: Avg of the Science, Creation, Logic and Game domain scores (GPT-4.1 key-point judge, 0-1).
setup.protocol: WEAVEBench: human-annotated multi-turn, in-context image editing and generation tasks (science, creation, logic, game) requiring visual memory and world knowledge; each editor produces the edited image from the original image and instruction history; GPT-4.1 judges key points against the reference image and the original image (hybrid VLM-judge, validated against three experts); Avg = mean over the four task domains. Editors are run in the partial in-context setting with image-only evaluation (row icons).
setup.limitations: Single VLM judge; benchmark images partly generated by Seedream 4.0, Nano Banana and SeedEdit 3.0; Seedream 4.0 and Nano Banana rows appear twice under different in-context settings and are not imported.

name: Knowledge Visualization T2I (Brief Caption, English overall)

setup.version: Knowledge Visualization benchmark as released with arXiv:2604.22302v1 (24 Apr 2026), Table 2 Brief Caption track
setup.metric: Mean checklist accuracy (Qwen2.5-VL-32B binary VQA) averaged over six subjects, English prompts; %, stored /100.
setup.protocol: Knowledge Visualization benchmark: 1,800 textbook-grounded science prompts (biology, chemistry, geography, history, math, physics; Chinese and English), Brief Caption track (abstract textbook caption, model must supply the knowledge); each image is checked against 4-6 expert-reviewed checklist items by Qwen2.5-VL-32B-Instruct as binary VQA; score = mean item accuracy; 'Overall en' = average over the six subjects on English prompts.
setup.limitations: Single open-weight MLLM judge; Chinese-prompt column and the Detailed Caption track (Table 5) are not imported.

setup.version: RealPref-Bench as released with arXiv:2604.19406v1 (21 Apr 2026), Table 1 'Human' column
setup.metric: Mean human score on the 0-5 rubric (0 = failure, 3 = instruction mostly followed but poor quality, 5 = full compliance with high quality); stored /5.
setup.protocol: RealPref-Bench: real-world images with manually verified edit instructions over eight sub-tasks (add, remove, object swap, background replace, colour, bokeh, relighting, style); user study (Sec. 5.4): five annotators score over 1k edited outputs per the 0-5 rubric (instruction adherence and image quality); 'Human' = average annotator score per model.
setup.limitations: Five annotators; the benchmark was built by the authors of an editing method (HP-Edit, not imported); HP-score columns (VLM scorer) not imported.

setup.version: SWITCH report v5 (7 Jul 2026), Table 3 single-image-to-video block, VLM-as-Judge Overall
setup.metric: Mean Gemini 3.1 Pro overall score on a 1-5 scale per video, stored /5 with chance 0.2.
setup.protocol: SWITCH generative track: image-to-video generation of tangible-interface interactions (e.g. operating light switches, appliance panels) from an initial frame plus a prompt fixing task type, next action, stop condition and required visible evidence; Gemini 3.1 Pro judges each video (1,170 valid evaluations) on scene fidelity, control correctness, procedure correctness and execution observability and gives a direct overall score on a 1-5 scale.
setup.limitations: Single VLM judge; the 160-video human evaluation in the same table reshuffles the ranking and is not imported; video-to-video block not imported. ShareAlike licence.

setup.version: WROP exam, arXiv:2609.28654v1 (23 Sep 2026), Table 2 human preference leaderboard (14 models)
setup.metric: Bradley-Terry Elo from 361 blind pairwise human judgments; 95% CI kept in notes.
setup.protocol: WROP exam: 300 object-permanence questions (six task families); each model receives the conditioning video prefix through its API's interface (true continuation, reference-to-video or frame-wise edit/transfer; Table 1) and its predicted continuation is trimmed to the target span; twenty raters made 361 blind pairwise judgments (50-52 per model, ties 0.5); Bradley-Terry maximum-likelihood Elo with one virtual draw per model.
setup.limitations: Small sample (about 52 games per model, wide CIs); models are reached through different API interfaces (continuation, reference-to-video, edit/transfer), so the test mixes capability with interface; ratings relative to this 14-model pool.

name: PROST physical reasoning (zero-shot, 10-concept macro average)
description: PROST (Aroca-Ouellette et al., Findings of ACL-IJCNLP 2021): 18,736 four-option multiple-choice questions from 14 templates over 10 physical concepts (direction, mass, height, circumference, stackable, rollable, graspable, breakable, slideable, bounceable), asked zero-shot. Score is the macro average of the 10 concept accuracies (multi-template concepts averaged first). Chance 0.25 as stated in the paper ('random guessing would yield an accuracy of 25%'). T5/UnifiedQA rows skip the sliding concept (asterisked 9-concept average) and are not comparable; UnifiedQA is also fine-tuned.

name: MT-Bench (GPT-4 single-answer grading, LMSYS runs)
metric: mean GPT-4 single-answer grade (1-10) over the 80 MT-Bench questions, both turns
description: MT-Bench (Zheng et al. 2023, arXiv 2306.05685): 80 two-turn open-ended questions in 8 categories (writing, roleplay, reasoning, math, coding, extraction, STEM, humanities); GPT-4 grades each answer 1-10 (single-answer grading, fastchat.llm_judge) and the score is the mean over all 160 turns. Raw judge-score units kept (kind linear, fixed latent_scale 1 = one MT-Bench point), not converted to accuracy. Only rows LMSYS published in its 2023 leaderboard tables (its own fastchat.llm_judge runs) are recorded; later rows whose values equal the makers' own announcements (e.g. Zephyr, Mixtral, Qwen1.5, Mistral 7B Instruct) are left out because LMSYS may have copied them.

name: MM-MT-Bench (Mistral, GPT-4o judge)
metric: mean judge grade (1-10) over the 92 MM-MT-Bench conversations
description: Multimodal MT-Bench (Mistral AI, Pixtral 12B paper Sec. 3; dataset mistralai/MM-MT-Bench, eval split): 92 conversations over charts, tables, PDF pages, diagrams and miscellaneous images (69 single-turn, 23 multi-turn); an independent LLM judge (GPT-4o in the paper's Table 2) grades each response 1-10 against a reference answer for correctness and completeness; score = mean grade. Raw judge units (kind linear, fixed latent_scale 1 = one point), not accuracy.

name: Ai2 Molmo human preference Elo (Sept 2024, 27 VLMs)
metric: Elo rating from Ai2's pairwise human preference study
description: Human preference evaluation run by Ai2 for the Molmo release (Deitke et al., arXiv 2409.17146): ~15k diverse image+text prompts were sent to 27 vision-language models, and ~870 annotators made ~325k pairwise preference judgments; ratings are Elo/Bradley-Terry scores published in the Molmo model cards ('Human Preference Elo Rating'). One fixed study (Sept 2024); not LMArena vision.

name: Ai2 Molmo2 human preference Elo (video/image QA, 2026)
metric: Bradley-Terry Elo from Ai2's pairwise human preference study
description: Human preference study run by Ai2 for the Molmo2 report (arXiv 2601.10611, Sec. 4.1): 450 manually filtered open-ended questions from annotators plus 51 video-captioning queries; two models' outputs are compared pairwise by annotators (over 105K ratings, 501 per model pair, 21 models); Elo via the Bradley-Terry model. Distinct from the Sept 2024 Molmo study and from LMArena.

name: Molmo2-CapTest dense video captioning F1
metric: statement-level F1 (LLM judge) vs human captions
description: Molmo2-CapTest (Ai2, arXiv 2601.10611): 693 Creative Commons videos, each with at least four human-written captions; an LLM judge scores the precision and recall of statements in the model's caption against the annotators' statements, reported as F1 (0-1).

name: Molmo2-VideoCount accuracy (val)
description: Molmo2-VideoCount (Ai2, arXiv 2601.10611): 533 diverse video counting questions (objects, actions, animals; up to 60 instances) built with the Molmo2-VideoPoint pipeline; accuracy = exact-count match on the val split.

name: HumanEvalExplain (HumanEvalPack, 6-language average)
description: HumanEvalPack explanation task (Muennighoff et al. 2023): the model explains a reference solution in natural language, then regenerates the code from its own explanation alone; pass@1 of the regenerated code, averaged over Python, JavaScript, Java, Go, C++ and Rust as printed by the source; greedy. Distinct from HumanEvalSynthesize and HumanEvalFix.

name: HumanEvalFix (HumanEvalPack, 6-language average)
description: HumanEvalPack bug-fixing task (Muennighoff et al. 2023): the model repairs a subtly buggy solution given failing unit tests; pass@1 averaged over Python, JavaScript, Java, Go, C++ and Rust as printed by the source; greedy. Distinct from HumanEvalSynthesize and HumanEvalExplain.

name: Paradee small-TTS comparison · 200 WikiText-103 sentences · UTMOS (utmos22_strong)
setup: Paradee report (arXiv:2610.06817v1) §5 and Table 3: each fixed-voice system reads the same 200 held-out English sentences (held out from a 12,000-sentence WikiText-103 corpus) in its own voice; naturalness predicted with UTMOS (utmos22_strong checkpoint), averaged over the 200 sentences. One author ran all systems.
display_unit: predicted MOS / 5; not human MOS, not accuracy
caveats: Automatic MOS predictor; the paper notes UTMOS missed an audible buzz artefact (§7, §9).
Each system uses a different voice (af_heart, lessac, Bella), so the score mixes voice and model quality.

name: Paradee small-TTS comparison · 200 WikiText-103 sentences · Whisper-base WER
setup: Same 200 held-out WikiText-103 sentences as paradee-wikitext200-utmos22; audio transcribed with Whisper (base) and compared with the source text (§5). WER % / 100.
caveats: Whisper base is a small ASR model; the paper says WER 'barely separates our models'.
Normalisation not stated.

name: carun tts-bench · 56-sentence English corpus · Whisper large-v3 WER
setup: carun/tts-bench (Apache-2.0): 56 English sentences in 7 categories (prose, numbers, acronyms, jargon, names, complex clauses, heteronyms) synthesised once per engine with its default/preset voice; each output transcribed by openai/whisper-large-v3 and scored against the input after the Whisper English normaliser on both sides; overall WER as printed in data/REPORT_DATA.md. The Parakeet-judge column is a correlated second ASR view of the same audio and is not recorded.
caveats: Small corpus (56 sentences, one seed); the author notes the heteronym category measures nothing.
Fixed-voice systems each use their own preset voice.

name: Wayu Thai TTS eval · English CER on 500 held-out LibriTTS lines (Whisper Large V3)
setup: Wayu/Paxa/Typhoon fixed-voice TTS report (arXiv:2609.03502v1) Table 8: each system synthesises 500 held-out LibriTTS English transcript lines with its Thai fixed/reference voice; audio transcribed with Whisper Large V3; mean CER in percent (divided by 100 here). Same evaluator and run as wayu-thai-cer500-typhoon-whisper.
caveats: Run by the makers of Wayu-Paxa-TTS-Edge, which was trained on LibriTTS transcripts (held-out lines are used for the test).
English intelligibility of Thai-voiced systems; complements the Thai CER of the same table rather than repeating it.

name: UltraText Bench (Composite, bilingual dense text rendering)

setup.version: UltraText Bench as released with arXiv:2610.09823v1 (7 Oct 2026), Table 5 leaderboard (24 model configurations)
setup.metric: Composite: 60/30/5/5 weighted Text Fidelity / Text Clarity / Spatial / Scene quality (Q-Judger ratings 0-100), prompt-macro mean per language, English and Chinese averaged equally; stored /100.
setup.protocol: 432 human-reviewed prompts (24 real-world scene categories in 6 domains, 3 difficulty levels L1 Hard / L2 Very Hard / L3 Extreme, 216 English + 216 Chinese), each with 4-12 exact target strings and a structured per-region reference (content, coarse position, carrier, visual attributes); prompt-only generation with each model's standard sampling configuration; Q-Judger VLM (from Qwen-Image-Bench) returns six image-level scores under the paper's rubric; accuracy+completeness form Fidelity, position+layout form Spatial.
setup.limitations: Single VLM judge (validated against ten human participants on a subset); model revisions, resolutions and API dates not published; execution failures lower coverage, not the quality mean; benchmark authors overlap with the LLaDA-Image team.

name: CREval-Bench creative image editing (Overall, GPT-4o QA evaluator)

setup.version: CREval-Bench as released with arXiv:2603.26174v1 (27 Mar 2026), Table 2
setup.metric: Overall avg: weighted average of Instruction Following, Visual Consistency and Visual Quality QA scores (0-100) over three creative editing types; stored /100.
setup.protocol: 800+ creative image-manipulation samples (Customization, Contextualization, Stylization; nine creative dimensions) with 13K automatically generated evaluation questions and reference answers; GPT-4o answers each question about the edited image and a matching answer earns the score; IF, VC and VQ aggregated by weighted average.
setup.limitations: Single MLLM evaluator (GPT-4o); per-model inference settings not tabulated; user study reports agreement with human judgments.

name: ServImage task acceptance (human payment decisions, commercial design tasks)

setup.version: ServImageBench as released with arXiv:2604.24023v2, Table 2 standard settlement scenario (16 models)
setup.metric: Task Acceptance: proportion of tasks whose deliverables are approved and paid under the original contract according to human payment-decision labels; stored as a fraction.
setup.protocol: 1,070 paid commercial design tasks collected from crowdsourcing platforms (271 portrait, 450 e-commerce product, 349 digital content; text-to-image and image-editing workflows; 2,046 required deliverables, $295k contract value); each model generates the required candidate deliverables from the brief, references and source image; human annotators label each candidate as approved/paid or not under the original contract.
setup.limitations: Mixes generation and editing tasks; editing-only models (SeedEdit) attempt all tasks; API tiers/quality settings not stated; ServImageModel-predicted variant (Table 9) not used.

name: HPSv3 image generation benchmark (Overall HPSv3 score)

setup.version: 'Image Generation Benchmark of HPSv3' table in the MizzenAI/HPSv3 README @bd0c5fc (11 models)
setup.metric: Overall: mean HPSv3 score of each model's generated images across 12 prompt categories (Characters, Arts, Design, Architecture, Animals, Natural Scenery, Transportation, Products, Others, Plants, Food, Science); raw units (about -0.2 to 10.6), higher is better; latent_scale 1 = one HPSv3 point.
setup.protocol: Images generated by the HPSv3 authors for their HPDv3 prompt sets and scored with the HPSv3 preference model (Qwen2-VL-7B with an uncertainty-aware ranking head).
setup.comparability: Automatic preference-model score, not human votes; HPSv3 was trained on HPDv3, which contains images from several of the benchmarked models. Do not pool with HPS v2 values.
setup.limitations: README does not list per-model sampling settings or prompt counts; the HPSv3 paper (arXiv 2508.03789) carries the default arXiv licence, so only the MIT README table is used.

setup.version: PAI-Bench-G as released with arXiv:2512.01989v1 (1 Dec 2025), Table 3 (15 VGMs)
setup.metric: Overall = average of Domain Score (MLLM QA accuracy on physical and semantic constraints) and Quality Score (subject/background consistency, motion smoothness, aesthetic and imaging quality, etc.), 0-100; stored /100.
setup.protocol: PAI-Bench-G real-world Physical-AI cases in six domains (common sense, autonomous vehicles, robotics, industry, human, physics); each model generates from the case caption and reference image (image-conditioned: the Quality Score includes Image-to-Video subject and background fidelity to the reference image) with default settings; open-source models averaged over five seeds per caption, Veo3 one video per caption.
setup.limitations: Automatic metrics plus MLLM judge; Generation settings are each model's defaults; CogVideoX/CogVideoX1.5 (T2V vs I2V checkpoint not stated), LTX-Video-2B (version not stated), Wan2.1-I2V-14B-720P, MAGI-1, DynamiCrafter and Cosmos-Predict rows not mapped.

setup.version: PAI-Bench-G human study, arXiv:2512.01989v1 Appendix Table 8 (8 systems incl. source videos)
setup.metric: Overall ELO aggregated from pairwise human preferences (video quality and physical plausibility, ties allowed) over videos generated from identical captions.
setup.protocol: Arena-based human study on PAI-Bench-G outputs; pairs sampled across models for the same caption.
setup.limitations: Number of participants and votes not given in the table; Generation settings are each model's defaults; CogVideoX/CogVideoX1.5 (T2V vs I2V checkpoint not stated), LTX-Video-2B (version not stated), Wan2.1-I2V-14B-720P, MAGI-1, DynamiCrafter and Cosmos-Predict rows not mapped.

name: CapArena-Auto detailed image captioning (Score_Avg, GPT-4o judge)

setup.version: CapArena-Auto leaderboard as printed in arXiv:2503.12329v1 Appendix J Table 8 (22 VLMs)
setup.metric: Score_Avg: mean over three baselines of the net pairwise score (+1 win, -1 loss, 0 draw) on 600 images, as printed on a -100..100 scale; raw units, latent_scale 50 (about one logit of win odds per 50 net points near parity).
setup.protocol: 600 DOCCI test images sampled from 149 clusters; detailed-caption prompt; each caption compared with GPT-4o, CogVLM2-llama3-chat-19B and MiniCPM-V2.6 captions by GPT-4o as judge with the human reference caption as support; 94.3% Spearman correlation with the CapArena human ranking (Table 3).
setup.limitations: Single VLM judge (GPT-4o) that is also a baseline and a contestant; caption length correlates with score; generation settings per model not tabulated.

setup.version: PhysBench test set as evaluated in arXiv:2501.16411v2 (Table 3 and Appendix Table 28, 75 VLMs)
setup.metric: Average accuracy over the four task categories (Property, Relationships, Scene, Dynamics); four-option multiple choice, chance 25%.
setup.protocol: 10,002 interleaved video-image-text multiple-choice entries; models evaluated with their own generation settings (Appendix Tables 9-11), with frames merged or sequential per model format.
setup.limitations: Mixed input formats (merge vs seq) per model; GPT-4o, Gemini 1.5 and Claude 3.5 Sonnet rows not mapped (snapshot not stated).

setup.version: MSEarth-Bench MCQ test split as evaluated in arXiv:2505.20740v3 (Table 4)
setup.metric: Overall accuracy on 2,784 four-option multiple-choice questions grounded in figures from Earth-science papers (single-image, multi-image and cross-image; reasoning and perception); chance 25%.
setup.protocol: Structured prompt per model; choice extracted with regular expressions; chat/instruction-tuned variants.
setup.limitations: Domain-specific (geoscience); GPT-4o version truncated in the paper and not mapped; Llama-3.2-90B-Vision path is the base checkpoint and not mapped.

setup.version: MMMG image-generation subset as evaluated in arXiv:2505.17613v2 (Appendix Table 9, 12 models)
setup.metric: Average accuracy over 15 image-generation tasks (object inclusion/exclusion/count/knowledge/commonsense/attribution, comparison and universal relations, relative/absolute spatial, region/border fill, single/double/multilingual text rendering); 0-1.
setup.protocol: Synthetic instructions per task; each task scored with the method best aligned with human judgment in the authors' validation (VLM-based or programmatic checks); API/HF checkpoints listed in Appendix C.
setup.limitations: Automatic evaluation; Janus Pro and BLIP-3o sizes not stated (not mapped).

name: MMMG knowledge-image generation (MMMG-Score, average over education levels)

setup.version: MMMG benchmark (4,456 prompts) as evaluated in arXiv:2506.10963v2, Table 2
setup.metric: MMMG-Score = knowledge fidelity (1 - GED between the reference knowledge graph and the subgraph that OpenAI-o3, high effort, grounds in the generated image) x a readability score from image segment counts, averaged over six education levels; x100 in the paper, stored /100.
setup.protocol: Knowledge-intensive explanatory-image prompts across 10 disciplines and six education levels; OpenAI-o3 grounds the expert-verified reference graph in each generated image.
setup.limitations: Automatic o3-based grounding (missing items count as false); distinct from the multitask MMMG benchmark (arXiv 2505.17613).

name: REAL realism benchmark for T2I (average of attribute, relationship and style scores)

setup.version: REAL benchmark as reported in arXiv:2502.10663v1, Table 5 (four T2I models)
setup.metric: Average of three realism scores in 0-1: attribute (share of visible schema attributes judged correctly depicted, normalised by visible attributes), relationship (objects and unusual relations present and realistic) and style (photorealistic rather than stylised), all from VQA queries.
setup.protocol: Prompts from 200 iNaturalist classes and 200 CUB-Birds classes (attributes, style) and UnRel unusual relationships; each image scored by a VQA model with REAL's schema; validated against MTurk annotations on 300 images.
setup.limitations: Only four models; SD 3.5 Turbo row not mapped (Large vs Medium not stated).

name: AlpacaEval 1.0 win rate (vs text-davinci-003, GPT-4 judge)
metric: win rate against text_davinci_003 on the 805 AlpacaEval instructions, judged by alpaca_eval_gpt4
description: AlpacaEval 1.0: the share of 805 instructions where a GPT-4 judge prefers the model's answer to text-davinci-003's. Not length-controlled; the reference scores 50% by definition.

name: Vectara hallucination leaderboard (HHEM-2.3, factual consistency rate)
metric: share of answered summaries judged factually consistent with the source document by HHEM-2.3
description: Each model summarises the same set of documents with a fixed prompt; Vectara's HHEM-2.3 classifier judges whether each summary is supported by its document. Factual consistency rate = 1 − hallucination rate, over the documents the model answered (answer rate reported separately).

name: Vectara hallucination leaderboard, 2025 dataset (HHEM-2.3, factual consistency rate)
metric: share of answered summaries judged factually consistent with the source document by HHEM-2.3
description: The leaderboard's previous document set (frozen October 2025): each model summarises the same documents with a fixed prompt and HHEM-2.3 judges whether each summary is supported. A different document set from the current leaderboard, so it is a separate test.

name: τ³-bench airline (tau2-bench ≥ v1.0.1)
description: Airline domain of τ³-bench (tau2-bench v1.0.1+, with the 75+ task fixes): pass^1. Not comparable with the original τ²-bench airline domain.

name: τ³-bench retail (tau2-bench ≥ v1.0.1)
description: Retail domain of τ³-bench (tau2-bench v1.0.1+, with the task fixes): pass^1. Not comparable with the original τ²-bench retail domain.

name: τ³-bench telecom (tau2-bench ≥ v1.0.1)
description: Telecom domain of τ³-bench (tau2-bench v1.0.1+): pass^1.

name: τ³-bench banking_knowledge (v1.0.1 grading)
description: Knowledge-retrieval banking domain of τ³-bench, graded with tau2-bench v1.0.1+ (the release notes say earlier banking scores are not comparable): pass^1.

name: CharXiv descriptive questions
description: CharXiv descriptive-question accuracy (validation set): reading basic elements of real scientific charts (titles, axes, labels, counts), graded by GPT-4o. The reasoning questions are a separate benchmark (charxiv-rq).

name: XTC-Bench generation (Overall Gen., scene-graph node agreement)

setup.metric: Overall Gen.: how well the image generated from a scene-graph-derived prompt recovers the scene-graph nodes (objects, attributes, relations) over all nodes, continuous 0-1.
setup.protocol: XTC-Bench derives generation prompts and understanding queries from the same structured scene graphs (COCO-based); generated images are parsed into scene graphs and matched to the reference with an LLM judge; Table 2 reports node-level generation quality. Eight open-source unified multimodal models run by the authors.
setup.limitations: Single LLM-judge pipeline; model checkpoints/resolutions not detailed in the main text; CCTA and understanding columns not recorded.

name: MixInstruct GPT-Rank (LLM-Blender, mean rank among 11 instruction-tuned LLMs, ChatGPT pairwise judge)

setup.version: MixInstruct test split, 4,771 examples (arXiv 2306.02561v3, Table 2)
setup.metric: GPT-Rank: each example's 11 candidate answers are ranked via ChatGPT pairwise comparisons (MaxWins aggregation); a model's score is its mean rank over examples (1 = best, 11 = worst).
setup.protocol: Eleven open instruction-following LLMs answer 100K MixInstruct prompts (Alpaca-GPT4, Dolly-15K, GPT4All-LAION, ShareGPT); ChatGPT compares all candidate pairs on the 4,771 test examples; checkpoints listed on the dataset card.
setup.limitations: Rank is pool-relative (11 models, mostly 2023 open models) and judged by ChatGPT; scale 1 = one rank position.

name: VMMU (Vietnamese multimodal understanding and reasoning, mean accuracy over 7 tasks)

setup.metric: Mean accuracy over the seven task columns of Table 2 (Math, Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Geography, Driving-license, IQ), stored as a fraction.
setup.protocol: 2.5k Vietnamese multimodal questions in 7 tasks; each question requires combining the image and text (no OCR/text-only shortcuts); models prompted with the paper's fixed prompt (Figs. 9-10); the paper prints a random-answer baseline row (mean 25.92%).
setup.limitations: Single prompt, API/open-weight inference settings not detailed; random baseline is 25.92% over the seven tasks (stored chance 0.2592).

name: Medmarks-V mean win rate (19 verifiable medical benchmarks, 71 configurations)

setup.version: Medmarks-V as run in arXiv 2605.01417v1 (61 models, 71 configurations)
setup.metric: Weighted mean win rate: for each of the 19 verifiable benchmarks a model's win rate is its share of pairwise wins against the other configurations; benchmarks are combined with log-size weights (appendix H).
setup.protocol: Open-source evaluation suite built on the verifiers library; open-weight models run on vLLM, API models through a gateway; each model evaluated with its officially recommended sampling parameters.
setup.limitations: Pool-relative (win rate against the 71-configuration pool), so scores shift if the pool changes; latent_scale 0.08 is the standard deviation (0.081) of the 71 published win rates (mean 0.50).

name: Cosmos 3D consistency: camera-pose estimation success rate on generated videos

setup.metric: Share of generated videos on which a structure-from-motion/pose estimator succeeds (higher = more geometrically consistent), stored as a fraction.
setup.protocol: NVIDIA's evaluation of base Cosmos models on 3D consistency (Sec. 5.2): videos generated from DAVIS-style prompts are reconstructed with a pose estimator; success rate and epipolar (Sampson) error are reported alongside view-synthesis metrics.
setup.limitations: Maker-run, four NVIDIA models only (plus VideoLDM and real-video reference rows not recorded); estimator and prompt set as in the paper.

name: Cosmos 3D consistency: Sampson epipolar error on generated videos (lower is better)

setup.metric: Mean Sampson (epipolar) error of correspondences between frames of the generated video; lower means more geometrically consistent.
setup.protocol: As cosmos-3d-pose-success: same videos, same table (Table 19).
setup.limitations: Raw error units; linear scale 0.1; four NVIDIA models only.

name: Kaleidoscope (in-language multimodal exams, 18 languages, overall accuracy)

setup.metric: Overall accuracy (Acc.) over all Kaleidoscope questions (multimodal and text-only), format errors counted as incorrect; stored as a fraction.
setup.protocol: 20,911 multiple-choice exam questions in 18 languages (55% need the image); zero-shot, answer extracted from <ANSWER> tags; open-weight models run locally with temperature 0.7, max 1024 tokens, 512x512 images; closed models use chain-of-thought prompts.
setup.limitations: Single prompt format; option counts vary by question so random-guess chance is not a single number (chance stored as 0).

name: Factual knowledge recall, Premium2k exact match (zero-shot)

setup.metric: Exact-match accuracy (zero-shot) on the 2,000-question Premium2k subset (fact-recall questions generated from Wikidata triplets with Wikipedia-grounded answers), stored as a fraction.
setup.protocol: 15k evaluation questions across 20 relation types, Premium2k = a 2k subset with manually verified, specific questions; zero-shot or 10-shot prompts per the paper's Tables 5-7; EM against the answer or its Wikidata aliases.
setup.limitations: Questions generated with Claude v1.3; sampling and API snapshots (July 2023) as in the paper; EM only (the 'Contains' column is not recorded).

setup.protocol: 15k evaluation questions across 20 relation types, Premium2k = a 2k subset with manually verified, specific questions; zero-shot or 10-shot prompts per the paper's Tables 5-7; EM against the answer or its Wikidata aliases.

name: CVTG-500L PNED (English long-prompt text rendering, Cosmos 3 report)

setup.metric: PNED: OCR-extracted text matched to target strings per region by Hungarian matching on normalised edit distance, English long-prompt set of 500 prompts; stored as a fraction.
setup.protocol: 500 prompts sampled from CVTG-2K (Du et al. 2025), each upsampled into a long dense description; OCR then PNED/GNED scoring (Sec. 6.2).
setup.limitations: Maker-run (NVIDIA) comparison of Cosmos 3 against open and closed models in one table; custom prompt sets (CVTG-500L, CVTG-102ch) are specific to the Cosmos 3 report.

name: CVTG-102ch PNED (Chinese character rendering, Cosmos 3 report)

setup.metric: PNED on a 102-prompt Chinese-character set; stored as a fraction.
setup.protocol: 102 NVIDIA-written prompts covering public spaces, outdoor scenes and digital displays; OCR + PNED as for CVTG-500L.
setup.limitations: Maker-run (NVIDIA) comparison of Cosmos 3 against open and closed models in one table; custom prompt sets (CVTG-500L, CVTG-102ch) are specific to the Cosmos 3 report.

name: HPSv3 score of Cosmos 3 report text-to-image evaluation images

setup.metric: Mean HPSv3 human-preference score of the images generated for the report's T2I benchmark prompts (raw HPSv3 units).
setup.protocol: Images generated by each model for the report's T2I prompts and scored by HPSv3.
setup.limitations: Maker-run (NVIDIA) comparison of Cosmos 3 against open and closed models in one table; custom prompt sets (CVTG-500L, CVTG-102ch) are specific to the Cosmos 3 report.

name: CodeReviewQA: automated code refinement, exact match rate

setup.metric: Overall exact-match rate (%) of the model's refined code against the human-refined reference over nine programming languages; stored as a fraction.
setup.protocol: CodeReviewQA (9 languages, review comments with code); zero-shot greedy generation, exact match after normalisation.
setup.limitations: Greedy single run; models listed in the paper's Table 7 only.

name: CodeReviewQA: change type recognition, invariant accuracy

setup.metric: Invariant accuracy (%) on the change-type-recognition multiple-choice probe: a question counts only if the model picks the right answer under every ordering of the options; stored as a fraction.
setup.protocol: MCQA probes derived from the same code-review items as the refinement task; log-probability ranking of the option symbols for every option ordering; zero-shot.
setup.limitations: Invariant accuracy is stricter than plain accuracy (chance is below 1/N, stored 0).

setup.limitations: Invariant accuracy is stricter than plain accuracy (chance is below 1/N, stored 0).

setup.metric: Invariant accuracy (%) on the hard solution-identification multiple-choice probe, order-invariant as above; stored as a fraction.

setup.metric: Accuracy column of Table 2: share of questions answered correctly (judge-checked) by the reasoning model, stored as a fraction.
setup.protocol: THINK-Bench: multidisciplinary reasoning questions with annotated key reasoning steps; eleven reasoning models queried once per question; Claude 3.7 Sonnet as step-matching and answer judge.
setup.limitations: Empty or answer-less outputs (common for DeepSeek distilled models) count as wrong; single judge model.

name: CEdit-Bench-EN overall (G_O, GPT-4o judge)
description: CEdit-Bench (introduced in the LongCat-Image report: 1,464 bilingual editing pairs across 15 task categories), English instructions, overall score G_O on the 0–10 VLM-judge scale (GPT-4o), divided by 10. Not GEdit-Bench.

name: CEdit-Bench-CN overall (G_O, GPT-4o judge)
description: CEdit-Bench Chinese-instruction track, overall score G_O on the 0–10 VLM-judge scale (GPT-4o), divided by 10. Separate from the English track.

name: OmniContext average (GPT-4.1 judge)
description: OmniContext (introduced in the OmniGen2 report): in-context, subject-driven generation from reference images over eight subtasks (single, multiple and scene; character, object and both). Average of the subtask overall scores (geometric mean of prompt following and subject consistency, GPT-4.1 judge, 0–10), divided by 10.
